title: Disproportionate Voices: Participation Inequality and Hostile Engagement in News Comments
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the prevalence of hate speech targeting specific groups, including religion, within South Korean online news comment sections. It used multi-label classification models to detect religious hate speech alongside other demographic targets (such as gender, race, and age) to analyze whether highly active users disproportionately post hostile content.
findings: Religion was analyzed as one of several core targets of online hate speech. The study found that hateful comments targeting religion frequently co-occur with hate speech targeting race/nationality. Overall, a small group of highly active commenters ('superusers') were found to disproportionately dominate online discourse and were significantly more likely to post hostile and hateful content—including religious hate speech—compared to infrequent commenters.
